name: Tattoo inks (permanent and temporary)
anchor: Strictest applicable sovereign FINISHED-COSMETIC contaminant maximum for technically unavoidable heavy-metal impurities, on a total-content basis (ug/kg of product as placed on market). The general tier is anchored by the German BVL 2017 orientation table; the only formulation splits in the family are the German make-up lead and theatrical-make-up arsenic branches and the Korean MFDS nickel product-class tiers, each preserved where the government wrote it. Tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures are anchored on EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13, an intradermal mixture instrument.
cross_reference: Permanent eyeliner, microblading and permanent lip pigment are permanent-make-up mixtures and belong in this row, not in the eye-makeup or lipstick rows. Topical body paints route to makeup-body-paints-bases-fixatives (row 6).
native_basis: finished leave-on cosmetic as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, not a migration or leachate value, and not a dietary basis. No reconstitution, dilution, or in-use concentration conversion is applied: the ceiling is compared to the product in the form the consumer buys it.
native_basis_label: Finished leave-on cosmetic, TOTAL CONTENT as placed on market (ug/kg of product as sold), on the technically-unavoidable-impurity basis every instrument in this family uses. Not a migration/leachate basis, not a dietary basis, not an ingredient purity specification.
scope_note: In scope: permanent tattoo inks and permanent-make-up pigments, including permanent eyeliner, microblading, scalp micropigmentation, areola and paramedical pigments, together with temporary topical tattoo products — transfer and decal tattoos, henna-style and jagua body art, and airbrush tattoo colours. Out of scope: topical body and theatrical paint (row 6) and needles, cartridges, tubes and grips, which are articles rather than mixtures and are not certified against a mixture ceiling. This row is the one place in Category 13 where the exposure route is INTRADERMAL rather than dermal, and it is governed by a distinct instrument family: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 with its Appendix 13 concentration limits, which apply to a mixture placed into the dermis rather than onto the stratum corneum. Because the taxonomy row also carries the temporary topical forms, which are cosmetics rather than intradermal mixtures and are not covered by the REACH entry, each cell names both the applicable REACH value and the applicable finished-cosmetic value and binds at the strictest of them. The result is mixed by analyte: REACH is stricter for lead and supplies the only nickel and Cr(VI) values, while the German cosmetic tier is stricter for cadmium and mercury. Three cells have no number from either instrument. Tin has no REACH row in the register and whether the entry's appendix sets a tin value has not been verified against the instrument, which is recorded as a register gap rather than filled from memory; aluminium and total chromium are unregulated in both families. All three are controls.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(color additive ingredient specification|colou?rant impurity|colourant impurity profile|colorant impurity))(?=.*(mixture for tattooing|permanent make-up|cosmetic|finished topical product)).*
basis_guard_note: This is the only row in the category whose guard admits the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up MIXTURE basis, because it is the only row whose product form that instrument governs. The guard admits two bases and no others: the intradermal tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis (EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13) for the row's permanent forms, and the finished-cosmetic total-content basis for the row's temporary topical forms. Both express a total mass fraction of the product as placed on market, so naming them in one cell mixes exposure routes but NOT bases, and the label on each cell records which instrument governs which form. Colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications, dietary maximum levels, and the textile and leather Cr(VI) extraction limits are all refused: the last of those is a migration basis and cannot anchor a total-content cell even though it is the only other sovereign Cr(VI) family in the register.
method: HMTc Method v2.0, government-limit-only initial setting: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact leave-on cosmetic form expressed as total content of the finished product as placed on market, or a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, or a substantiated not-material determination, or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, no cell is precautionary or feasibility-adjusted, and no cell is anchored on an ingredient or colour-additive purity specification.

Pb.basis: Total content of the product as placed on market (ug/kg): the intradermal mixture basis for the row's permanent forms, the finished-cosmetic basis for its temporary topical forms. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Pb.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75, Appendix 13: lead in a tattooing or permanent-make-up mixture, 700 ug/kg (0.00007 percent by weight).
Pb.substantiation: The EU value of 700 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign lead maximum for either form in this row and it binds. It comes from the instrument that directly regulates the exact product form — a mixture for tattooing or permanent make-up — and the register records its derivation from the Appendix 13 specific concentration limit of 0.00007 percent by weight. The finished-cosmetic instruments applicable to the row's temporary topical forms are named alongside it (Germany 2000, China 10000, Health Canada 10000, Taiwan 10000) and are all looser, so the row's ceiling is protective for every form in it. Intradermal placement bypasses the stratum corneum entirely and there is no dermal-absorption discount to apply, which is why the tattoo instrument is stricter than the cosmetic tier for this analyte.

Cd.basis: Total content of the product as placed on market (ug/kg): the intradermal mixture basis for the row's permanent forms, the finished-cosmetic basis for its temporary topical forms. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Cd.label: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic cadmium value, 100 ug/kg — stricter than the EU tattoo-mixture value of 500 and applicable to this row's temporary topical forms.
Cd.substantiation: The EU tattoo and permanent-make-up value is 500 ug/kg, from the Appendix 13 specific concentration limit of 0.00005 percent by weight, and it directly regulates the row's permanent forms. The German general cosmetic value of 100 ug/kg directly regulates the row's temporary topical forms, which are cosmetics and are not covered by the REACH entry. Because one published ceiling has to be protective for every form certified against the row, the row binds at 100 ug/kg. That is five-fold stricter than the EU's own tattoo-ink value, which is disclosed over-compliance for the permanent forms rather than a claim that the EU requires it.

tAs.basis: Total content of the product as placed on market (ug/kg): the intradermal mixture basis for the row's permanent forms, the finished-cosmetic basis for its temporary topical forms. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tAs.label: EU REACH Appendix 13 tattoo and permanent-make-up arsenic value, 500 ug/kg, which coincides exactly with the German general cosmetic value of 500 for the row's temporary topical forms.
tAs.substantiation: Both instruments applicable to this row set 500 ug/kg total arsenic: the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up entry (Appendix 13, 0.00005 percent by weight, recorded as total arsenic because the instrument does not speciate) and the German general cosmetic branch. The coincidence means no aggregation judgement is needed for this analyte. China NMPA 2015 and Kenya KS 2937:2021 at 2000 are named and are looser. The instrument does not speciate arsenic, so the inorganic-arsenic cell on this row is a control bounded by this total-arsenic value.

iAs.rationale: Neither instrument governing this row speciates arsenic. The EU tattoo and permanent-make-up entry sets a total-arsenic concentration limit and the register records it as tAs for that reason, and no jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic maximum for a tattoo mixture, a permanent-make-up pigment or any finished cosmetic. A total cannot be converted into a species and species never satisfy totals, so no number is invented. Inorganic arsenic matters more here than anywhere else in the category, because the mineral and metal-oxide pigments that carry it are placed permanently into the dermis rather than onto it, so speciation is mandatory.
iAs.reference_method: Arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS, or an equivalent validated speciation method, on the finished ink or pigment, reported on the certificate alongside the mandatory total-arsenic result. Inorganic arsenic is bounded above by the published 500 ug/kg total-arsenic ceiling by identity. Escalation: an inorganic-arsenic result that alone reaches the published total-arsenic ceiling is a hard stop; an inorganic fraction rising materially against the pigment's established baseline triggers pigment-lot traceback and CAPA.

companions.basis: mixture for tattooing or permanent make-up by weight; source unit percent by weight
companions.scope: mixtures for use for tattooing or permanent make-up

tHg.basis: Total content of the product as placed on market (ug/kg): the intradermal mixture basis for the row's permanent forms, the finished-cosmetic basis for its temporary topical forms. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
tHg.label: Germany BVL 2017 general cosmetic total-mercury value, 100 ug/kg — stricter than the EU tattoo-mixture value of 500 and applicable to this row's temporary topical forms.
tHg.substantiation: The EU tattoo and permanent-make-up value is 500 ug/kg, from the Appendix 13 specific concentration limit of 0.00005 percent by weight. The German general cosmetic value of 100 ug/kg applies to the row's temporary topical forms, which are cosmetics, and it is five-fold stricter. The row binds at 100 ug/kg so that one published ceiling is protective for every form in it; that is disclosed over-compliance for the permanent forms. The US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 adulteration rule (1000) and China NMPA 2015 (1000) are named and are looser. Mercury-bearing pigments, historically cinnabar-based reds, are the reason this cell is not academic.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it by identity, and a leave-on cosmetic matrix supplies no methylation pathway: biotic mercury methylation requires the sulfate- and iron-reducing microbial activity of anoxic aquatic sediment, which has no analogue in an anhydrous, emulsified or preserved cosmetic formulation. Mercury reaches a cosmetic either as an unintentional inorganic trace carried by mineral raw materials or, in the jurisdictions that still permit it, as an organomercurial preservative (thiomersal, phenylmercuric salts) — and neither of those is methylmercury. The published total-mercury ceiling on this row therefore bounds methylmercury completely, so no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: No routine methylmercury assay is required. Total mercury by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave digestion is mandatory on every lot and bounds methylmercury by identity. Reflex: methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or an equivalent validated method is required before this determination may be relied on for a lot, wherever the formulation declares a marine-derived, fish-derived or algal-derived ingredient, and for any lot whose total mercury exceeds the published ceiling.
MeHg.substantiation: The determination is bounded, not merely asserted: total mercury is measured on every lot and methylmercury cannot exceed it, so the not-material claim carries a published numeric bound at all times. The marine-, fish- and algal-ingredient reflex closes the only route by which pre-formed methylmercury could enter a cosmetic, which is a contaminated ingredient rather than in-matrix formation.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any cosmetic. Every mercury instrument in this family regulates total mercury: Germany BVL 2017 (100 ug/kg), US FDA 21 CFR 700.13 (1000 ug/kg, calculated as elemental mercury), China NMPA 2015, Health Canada, Taiwan MOHW 2024, Korea MFDS, Hong Kong Cap. 640, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive with its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937:2021 and the EAEU technical regulation. The EU prohibits mercury and its compounds as cosmetic ingredients outright under Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II without publishing any speciated value, and the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up restriction likewise sets a total-mercury value only.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 1223/2009 Annex II; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 Appendix 13; Germany BVL 2017; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance and topical natural-health-product limits; China NMPA 2015; Taiwan MOHW 2024; Korea MFDS Notices 2024-9 and 2025-63; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 with the Indonesian, Malaysian, Singaporean and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020 and IS 3959:2004; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; Hong Kong Cap. 640; New Zealand HSR002552; South Africa GN R.1227. None publishes a methylmercury value for a cosmetic.

Ni.basis: Total content of the product as placed on market (ug/kg): the intradermal mixture basis for the row's permanent forms, the finished-cosmetic basis for its temporary topical forms. Not migration, not leachate, not dietary, not an ingredient purity specification.
Ni.label: EU REACH Appendix 13 tattoo and permanent-make-up nickel value, 5000 ug/kg (0.0005 percent by weight).
Ni.substantiation: The EU tattoo and permanent-make-up nickel value of 5000 ug/kg is the strictest applicable value for either form in this row and it binds. The Korean 'other cosmetics' branch at 10000 ug/kg applies to the row's temporary topical forms and is named alongside it; it is twice as loose. Nickel is the analyte where intradermal placement is most consequential, because nickel sensitisation is the most common metal allergy and a permanent tattoo is a lifelong intradermal depot, which is why the EU wrote a tattoo-specific value at all.

Sn.rationale: The register carries no tin row for the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up entry, and no jurisdiction publishes a tin maximum for a finished cosmetic either, so neither instrument governing this row supplies a tin number. Whether Appendix 13 sets a tin concentration limit for these mixtures has NOT been verified against the instrument, and the register carries no tin row for the entry; this standard does not fill a cell from recollection, so the question is recorded as a register gap for resolution through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and the cell is a control in the meantime. If a sovereign tin value is confirmed and ingested, this cell is re-derived as a numeric cell. The register's other tin values are dietary maximum levels and food-contact or skin-contact organotin limits, in bases that cannot anchor a total-content mixture cell. Tin is a real presence here through tin-oxide pigments and organotin stabiliser residues in ink carriers.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, with organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS wherever a tin-bearing pigment or an organotin-stabilised carrier is declared. Escalation: a total-tin result above the pigment's established baseline triggers pigment and carrier traceback and CAPA. The cell is re-derived as a numeric cell as soon as the Appendix 13 tin value is ingested and verified.

Al.rationale: Neither instrument governing this row sets an aluminium maximum: the EU tattoo and permanent-make-up entry lists no aluminium value, and no jurisdiction publishes an aluminium maximum for a finished cosmetic. There is no near-neighbour cell to read across from. Aluminium is nonetheless intrinsic to this product form rather than incidental, because aluminium-lake pigments and alumina substrates are standard ink chemistry, so a single contaminant ceiling would be meaningless while the metal cannot go unmeasured.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-OES or ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot, reported together with the declared aluminium-bearing pigments and substrates so the measured burden can be reconciled against the formulation. Escalation: an aluminium result the declared formulation cannot account for triggers pigment traceback and CAPA, because unexplained aluminium indicates an undeclared lake or filler, which is also a common carrier of the lead this row does cap.

Cr.rationale: Neither instrument governing this row sets a total-chromium maximum. The EU tattoo and permanent-make-up entry regulates chromium only as Cr(VI), which is the deliberate and correct choice: total chromium in an ink is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from chromium-oxide and chromium-hydroxide green pigments, so a total-chromium ceiling would not be protective as a standalone number. No jurisdiction publishes a total-chromium maximum for a cosmetic either. Total chromium is therefore carried as the mandatory screen that governs the Cr(VI) reflex on this row, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion, every lot. It is the screen, not a pass/fail ceiling. A total-chromium result above the pigment's established baseline, or the declaration of any chromium-bearing pigment, mandates Cr(VI) speciation against this row's published Cr(VI) ceiling. Escalation: unexplained total-chromium elevation triggers pigment traceback and CAPA.

Cr-VI.basis: Total content of the mixture as placed on market (ug/kg), intradermal mixture basis. Not a migration or extraction value: the textile and leather Cr(VI) limits in the register are extraction limits and are refused by this row's basis guard.
Cr-VI.label: EU REACH Appendix 13 tattoo and permanent-make-up hexavalent-chromium value, 500 ug/kg (0.00005 percent by weight) — the only sovereign Cr(VI) maximum for a cosmetic-family product form anywhere in the register.
Cr-VI.substantiation: This is the single numeric Cr(VI) cell in Category 13, and it exists because the EU legislated a hexavalent-chromium concentration limit for tattooing and permanent-make-up mixtures. The register records it from the Appendix 13 entry, where chromium is listed with a footnote specifying Cr(VI) at 0.00005 percent by weight. No finished-cosmetic instrument in any jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI) value, which is why every other row in this category carries a Cr(VI) control instead of a number; that asymmetry is a real feature of the law and not an artefact of this build. The value is applied to the row's temporary topical forms as well as its permanent forms, which is stricter than those forms' own instruments require, because there is no cosmetic Cr(VI) value to compare it against and the row must publish one protective ceiling.
